newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Rupiah, ringgit on roller coaster.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Rupiah, ringgit on roller coaster.

text.p: The Malaysian ringgit and Indonesian rupiah jumped in early Friday trade as swap points soared and a liquidity squeeze triggered liquidation of long dollar positions, dealers said.

The ringgit's rise was escalated by talk Bank Negara Malaysia had asked local banks to stop quoting tom/next to offshore parties, a move that would mirror what the Thai central bank did on Thursday in an effort to squeeze out speculators.
Confirmation was not immediately available from Bank Negara.
Analysts say the market has been surprised by the way the region's central banks have been able to cut liquidity to the offhshore markets without impacting on domestic interbank rates.
They said this has been achieved by exerting moral suasion on domestic banks not to lend money to offshore players.
A U.S. bank dealer in Singapore said tom/next on the ringgit was trading as high as 300. "That's like a 500 percent interest rate," he said.
Dealers said overseas funds were being forced to sell dollars in the spot market to cover their short ringgit and rupiah positions.
"A lot of funds are cutting their long dollar positions. It's a blood bath. The funds have been hurt very badly," the dealer said.
The ringgit rose to a high of 2.4750 against the dollar in early trade against its opening around 2.4900. It was quoted at 2.4900/20 at 0235 GMT.
In Jakarta, market talk that Malaysian authorities planned to scrap swap facilities caused offshore players to flood the Indonesian swap market, pushing the rupiah to a high of 2,413.0.

"There are a lot of rumours in the market. We don't know what is true. But people are saying swap facilities could be scrapped in Malaysia, triggering a slew of switches to Indonesia," a Jakarta dealer said.
By 0235 GMT, the rupiah had slipped back to 2,430.0/35.0 but was still well above its opening 2,440.0/45.0.
Meanwhile, the Thai baht remained relatively firm but off its highs, at around the 25.450/25.650 to the dollar at 0235 GMT against a high of 25.300/25.340 late on Thursday.

Singapore dealers said the tom/next rate had also settled down after rising to a peak of 200 satangs on Thursday, but rumours that Thai banks were still not being allowed to quote tom/next to offshore players persisted.
"There seems to be a concerted move by central banks to squeeze out the speculators," a European bank dealer in Singapore said.

"Generally the speculative, especially the U.S. hedge funds and short-term European funds are learning a lesson, which is not a bad thing. But in the short term, it could have a negative impact on foreign direct investment," he added.
Dealers said money market liquidity in Singapore had also tightened in what appeared to be a spillover effect from the volatility in other centres.
The release of Singapore's first quarter gross domestic product and other economic indicators was largely eclipsed by the activity in the ringgit and rupiah, dealers said.
The Singapore dollar was quoted at 1.4321/31 at 0235 GMT.
-- Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221-384-6364) and Sonali Desai in Singapore
